assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and reset are modeled as discrete events because the NL describes them as triggers/signals rather than persistent declared variables.
hbrg is encoded as int values: 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop.
Outstanding request context is not stored because no request memory variables or queuing behavior were specified; requests are checked as events while stopped at floor states.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatches to F1 stopped, then PS2 drives upward to MU2, S2 stops at F2, and immediate next PS3 request drives upward to MU3.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_to_f2_then_continue_up

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F1 checks that PS3 selects MU3 upward motion and S3 arrival stops at F3.
scenario_results.name: f1_request_f3_and_arrive

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F2 checks that PS1 selects MD1 downward motion and S1 arrival stops at F1.
scenario_results.name: f2_request_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F3 checks that PS2 selects MD2 downward motion and S2 arrival stops at F2.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_down_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F3 checks the distinct PS1 branch to MD1 and S1 arrival at floor 1.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_direct_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in upward motion MU3 checks that reset forces the controller back to F1 stopped regardless of request context.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_upward_motion_forces_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F3 checks that reset also forces the controller back to F1 stopped from a floor state.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_floor3_forces_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F2 checks that without a request or arrival event the stopped floor state remains F2 with stop hbrg.
scenario_results.name: stopped_floor_no_event_holds

evidence: NL: state space combines F1/F2/F3 with MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2.
DSL declares states F1, F2, F3, MU2, MU3, MD1, MD2.
NL: From F1, PS2 triggers MU2 and PS3 triggers MU3; DSL includes F1 -> MU2 :: PS2 and F1 -> MU3 :: PS3.
NL: Arrival sensors complete motion transitions; DSL includes MU2 -> F2 :: S2, MU3 -> F3 :: S3, MD1 -> F1 :: S1, MD2 -> F2 :: S2.
NL: reset forces controller back to floor 1; DSL includes ! * -> F1 :: reset.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the explicit NL FSM: all named floor states, motion states, request-triggered dispatch transitions, sensor arrival transitions, reset-to-F1 behavior, and hbrg drive/stop outputs are represented.

NL describes hbrg as an output distinguishing upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
findings.summary: Required structural components are covered: states, transitions, input events, reset, and hbrg output actions are present. The unreferenced hbrg diagnostic is acceptable because hbrg is modeled as an output, not a guard-driving internal variable.

evidence: NL: stops at the requested floor, and then immediately checks the next destination before deciding whether to continue moving.
NL: reset signal forces the controller back to floor 1 regardless of the outstanding request context.
GroundingMap.source_summary assumption: Outstanding request context is not stored because no request memory variables or queuing behavior were specified.
DSL has no request memory variables or queued-request guards; transitions from floor states are direct PS1/PS2/PS3 events.
findings.summary: The phrase 'immediately checks the next destination' and the reset reference to 'outstanding request context' could imply persistent request memory or queued destinations, but the DSL treats requests as instantaneous events only while stopped. This is a scope/interpretation gap rather than a clear contradiction because the NL also enumerates event-triggered floor transitions directly.

evidence: DSL contains one output variable hbrg and no request queue/latch variables.
Transitions are limited to the ten NL-specified request/arrival transitions plus initial/reset behavior.
sim_summary scenarios are positive-path oriented and do not exercise simultaneous or conflicting inputs.
findings.summary: The model intentionally implements the elevator as the enumerated seven-state FSM and does not model richer elevator concerns such as simultaneous requests, request latching during motion, door/open-close behavior, or invalid sensor combinations. These are not explicitly required by the NL, so this is advisory only.

evidence: DSL: ! * -> F1 :: reset.
DSL: state F1 enter { hbrg = 0; }.
sim_summary includes reset_from_upward_motion_forces_f1 and reset_from_floor3_forces_f1, both passing with hbrg = 0.
findings.summary: No unsafe recovery issue detected within the stated NL scope. Reset is global and returns to F1 with hbrg stop output through F1 enter action, matching the reset requirement.
